introduction: These readings are letters about one thing: whether, and when, a believer may travel to the presence of Bahá’u’lláh or ‘Abdu’l-Bahá or to the Shrines in the Holy Land. Some grant leave warmly; many ask the writer to wait, because the road is unsafe, the summer unhealthy, the authorities watchful, or because the person is needed where they are, teaching; some forbid coming without permission, since unlooked-for arrivals had harmed the community; some accept a pilgrimage made by proxy, or call a longing itself a visit; and the last welcome those who arrived and send them home. A hundred of the guide's three hundred quotations are read here, ten from each tenth of the reading order, beside a hundred from elsewhere. Most stand alongside: the psalms of the road to Jerusalem, the Qur'an's call to the House, Esther and the golden sceptre, Paul's letters about visits longed for and hindered, the healed man told to go home to his friends, the queen of Sheba, Naaman's two mule-loads of earth. Eight push back or add a side: Kabir's God who is in neither temple nor Kaaba, Paul and Solomon on a God no house contains, Emerson on the indifference of places, 'suffer the children and forbid them not', the boldness Hebrews asks for, Mary's good part beside the instruction to stay and serve, and the cross beside the insistence on a safe and comfortable journey.
questions: Why, on the evidence of these letters, did a visit need permission? List the reasons given for saying 'not now'.
Many are told that teaching where they are matters more than coming. Set this beside Jesus's words to the healed man, and to Martha about Mary. When is presence the better part?
Kabir, Paul and Emerson doubt that God is found by going somewhere. What do the readings say a pilgrim receives?
A pilgrimage made by a deputy, or only intended, is accepted. What does that say about what pilgrimage is?
The letters ask for journeys made 'with the utmost joy' and in safety. What would Jesus's call to take up a cross add or question?
What does a pilgrim owe to those at home on returning?

outside.why: A pilgrim psalm asks: as the hart panteth after the water brooks, when shall I come and appear before God?
A psalm blesses those in whose heart are the ways, who pass through the dry valley and go from strength to strength.
Paul writes to a church he has never visited: I long to see you, that I may be comforted together with you.
Esther knew the rule of the Persian court: no one comes to the king uncalled, unless he hold out the golden sceptre.
The Qur'an makes pilgrimage to the House a duty for whoever can find a way there.
A psalm of ascent says: I was glad when they said unto me, let us go into the house of the Lord.
Abraham is told in the Qur'an to proclaim the pilgrimage, and that they will come on foot and on every lean camel.
Kabir has God ask: where dost thou seek me? I am beside thee; I am neither in temple nor in mosque, neither in Kaaba nor in Kailash. What does a pilgrim find that is not at home?
Certain Greeks who had come up to the feast came to a disciple and said: Sir, we would see Jesus.
Jesus said: him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.
The centurion told Jesus there was no need to come under his roof: speak the word only.
Jacob woke in a bare place and said: surely the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not.
At Sinai Moses was told to set bounds round the mountain, for the people's own safety.
Jesus told his brothers, who urged him to go up to the feast: my time is not yet come.
When disciples turned children away, Jesus said: suffer them, and forbid them not, to come unto me. When is it right to keep the eager away, and who bears the cost?
Moses at the bush was told: draw not nigh hither; put off thy shoes, for the place is holy ground.
Hebrews invites: let us come boldly unto the throne of grace. How do boldness and waiting for leave belong together?
Acts tells of an Ethiopian official who had come all the way to Jerusalem to worship, and was reading Isaiah as he returned.
Philip answered a friend who doubted that any good could come from Nazareth with three words: come and see.
A psalm counsels: wait on the Lord; be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart.
Ecclesiastes says that to every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose.
Paul and his companions were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to go one way, and so were led another.
Paul once planned his voyage so as to be at Jerusalem for the day of Pentecost.
Luke says the parents of Jesus went up to Jerusalem every year at the feast, with the crowds.
Paul tells the Romans he has been much hindered from coming to them, but hopes to see them on his journey.
Habakkuk is told of the vision: though it tarry, wait for it, because it will surely come.
Lamentations says it is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait.
Paul tells the Thessalonians that he tried to come to them once and again, and was hindered.
Jesus said that whoever would come after him must take up his cross. These letters make safety and comfort a condition of coming: what does that show about the one who writes them?
Jacob is promised: I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again.
Jesus told his followers to pray that their flight be not in the winter.
A psalmist says: my soul waiteth for the Lord more than they that watch for the morning.
Jesus said to Thomas: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
Paul put off a visit to Corinth: I will tarry at Ephesus, for a great door is opened, and there are many adversaries.
The elder writes that he would not say all with paper and ink: I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face.
Paul says he was taken from his friends in presence, not in heart, and longed the more to see their face.
Milton concluded that thousands speed at God's bidding, and they also serve who only stand and wait.
Emerson called travelling a fool's paradise, since our first journeys discover to us the indifference of places. What does a pilgrim hope to find that he does not carry with him?
Isaiah foresees many people saying: come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord.
Zechariah foresees ten men of all languages taking hold of one pilgrim's skirt: we will go with you.
Rumi's reed-flute laments its banishment from its home, the osier bed from which it was torn.
Proverbs knows what delay costs: hope deferred maketh the heart sick, but when the desire cometh it is a tree of life.
Proverbs says that a man's heart deviseth his way, but the Lord directeth his steps.
A man Jesus had healed begged to go with him; Jesus suffered him not, and said: go home to thy friends, and tell them.
Paul desired to depart and be with Christ, but judged that to remain was more needful for his friends.
Jesus said the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
When Martha served and Mary sat listening, Jesus said Mary had chosen the good part. Here service at a distance is preferred to presence: how do the two judgments fit?
The servant in the parable is first faithful over a few things, and then told: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.
Isaiah heard the question 'whom shall I send?' and answered: here am I; send me.
A psalm advises: commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him, and he shall bring it to pass.
The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came a great distance to prove it for herself.
A psalmist says: one thing have I desired of the Lord, that I may dwell in his house and behold his beauty.
Ruth would not be left behind: whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge.
In the parable a widow keeps coming to a judge until he gives way.
Jesus received a woman others would have turned away, saying that she loved much.
The Song of Songs has the beloved say: by night I sought him whom my soul loveth; I sought him, but I found him not.
Jesus said: ask, and it shall be given you; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Jacob wrestled until the breaking of the day and said: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
Isaiah has God promise: before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
Paul's friends begged him not to go up to Jerusalem; he answered that he was ready to be bound and to die there.
The law of the pilgrim feasts adds a condition: they shall not appear before the Lord empty.
Balaam says that God is not a man, that he should lie, nor the son of man, that he should repent.
Of ten who were healed, one turned back and fell at Jesus' feet, giving him thanks.
A psalmist says that a day in God's courts is better than a thousand.
The elder writes that he has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth.
A travellers' psalm promises: the Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in.
Abraham was called to go alone, from his kindred and his father's house.
Luke says that when the time was come, Jesus stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem.
The traveller on the desert road asked: see, here is water; what doth hinder me?
A psalm says: my soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the Lord.
The Song of Songs calls at the turn of the year: the winter is past; arise, and come away.
Paul too signed a letter himself, so that it could not be doubted: the salutation by the hand of me Paul.
Isaiah promises travellers: ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace.
A psalm says: serve the Lord with gladness; come before his presence with singing.
Solomon, dedicating the temple, asked whether God will indeed dwell on the earth, when the heaven of heavens cannot contain him. What is visited when a holy threshold is visited?
Jesus said: come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
A psalm says: my soul thirsteth for thee, in a dry and thirsty land, to see thy power and thy glory.
A psalm prays: send out thy light and thy truth; let them bring me unto thy holy hill.
Paul told the Athenians that the Lord of heaven and earth dwelleth not in temples made with hands. Why circle a place, if God is not held in one?
Augustine says to God: you have made us for yourself, and our hearts are restless until they rest in you.
Hebrews says that Abraham went out, not knowing whither he went, and sojourned as in a strange country.
Paul writes of a helper who might have ministered to him in his friend's stead.
Naaman, who could not stay, asked to carry home two mules' burden of the land's earth.
Paul tells the Colossians that though absent in the flesh, he is with them in the spirit.
Simeon in the temple said: mine eyes have seen thy salvation; now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.
Jesus said the hour was coming when worship would be neither on this mountain nor at Jerusalem, but in spirit and in truth.
David wished to build a house for God and could not; he was told: thou didst well that it was in thine heart.
A psalmist asks: whither shall I go from thy spirit? If I dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea, thou art there.
Matthew tells of wise men who came from the east, a long road, to see one child.
The queen of Sheba said on arriving: I believed not the words until I came; the half was not told me.
Paul lists what his journeys cost: thrice shipwrecked, in perils of waters, in weariness and painfulness.
Jesus told his disciples: blessed are your eyes, for they see what many prophets desired to see.
When the wise men saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
Peter, realizing whom he was with, fell down at Jesus' knees and called himself a sinful man.
A psalm says that they that go down to the sea in ships see the wonders of the Lord in the deep.
Proverbs says that children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers.
The Ethiopian traveller, his meeting on the road over, saw his teacher no more, and went on his way rejoicing.
Zacchaeus sought to see Jesus, could not for the press, and ran ahead and climbed a tree.
The shepherd psalm says: thou preparest a table before me; my cup runneth over.
Luke's Gospel ends with the disciples returning to Jerusalem with great joy, praising and blessing God.

esther-golden-sceptre.text: All the king's servants, and the people of the king's provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or women, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live

exodus-set-bounds.text: And thou shalt set bounds unto the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, that ye go not up into the mount, or touch the border of it: whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death

quran-proclaim-the-pilgrimage.text: And proclaim unto mankind the pilgrimage. They will come unto thee on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep ravine,

quran-pilgrimage-to-the-house.text: Wherein are plain memorials (of Allah's guidance); the place where Abraham stood up to pray; and whosoever entereth it is safe. And pilgrimage to the House is a duty unto Allah for mankind, for him who can find a way thither. As for him who disbelieveth, (let him know that) lo! Allah is Independent of (all) creatures.

thessalonians-satan-hindered-us.text: But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavoured the more abundantly to see your face with great desire. Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us

luke-went-up-to-jerusalem-every-year.text: Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover. And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast

john-we-would-see-jesus.text: And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast: The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus

acts-eunuch-came-to-worship.text: And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet

acts-went-on-his-way-rejoicing.text: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing

genesis-i-am-with-thee-whither-thou-goes.text: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of

kings-two-mules-burden-of-earth.text: And Naaman said, Shall there not then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules' burden of earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord

philemon-in-thy-stead.text: Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel: But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly

luke-returned-with-great-joy.text: And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy: And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God

psalm-in-whose-heart-are-the-ways.text: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them. Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools. They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God

john-in-no-wise-cast-out.text: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out

john-my-time-is-not-yet-come.text: Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready. The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil. Go ye up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast: for my time is not yet full come

psalm-wait-on-the-lord.text: Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord

corinthians-tarry-at-ephesus.text: For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit. But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost. For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries

deuteronomy-three-times-appear.text: Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before the Lord empty

luke-zacchaeus-sought-to-see.text: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature. And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way

acts-hasted-to-be-at-jerusalem.text: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost

luke-set-his-face-to-jerusalem.text: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem

john-touch-me-not.text: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father

emerson-travelling-is-a-fools-paradise.text: Travelling is a fool's paradise. Our first journeys discover to us the indifference of places
emerson-travelling-is-a-fools-paradise.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

kings-well-that-it-was-in-thine-heart.text: And the Lord said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart

proverbs-hope-deferred.text: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life
